title: Akai Ito

routes.title: 千羽烏月ルート
routes.notes: Senba Uzuki (千羽烏月, VNDB c10500). Reachable from the start; True End is『爽やかな立ち風』（ED32）, with ED3/13/28/29/30/31 as alternate endings. The original PS2 release and HD Remaster are treated as the same route system absent concrete behavioral-change evidence. The guide's main opening uses the Livedoor/Foxtail-supported『わたしはこくりと頷いた』path; XNEO's early-choice variants are treated as alternate valid routing, not a release difference. ED13『赤い縛め』requires an earlier no-chase state. Because no usable source-documented checkpoint exists before that required branch, ED13 is represented as a complete replay-from-beginning failed-play prefix using『追いかけない → 納得できない → 別に』, then the main Uzuki run begins fresh. Foxtail explicitly says the later night choice is absent when Uzuki was not met, so Livedoor's Save②『別に → 歯磨きはオッケー？』recovery combines incompatible branch states and is treated as a walkthrough error. XNEO/Lastcharles list an extra phone choice after the no-chase branch; because Foxtail marks『別に』itself as No.13 and says the later prompt is suppressed in that state, the guide treats that trailing phone entry as over-specified recovery shorthand rather than a required action. All six documented Uzuki save checkpoints remain on the main run.

routes.title: 若杉葛ルート
routes.notes: Wakasugi Tsuzura (若杉葛, VNDB c10498). Nintendo Switch アカイイト HD REMASTER target. True End ED12 requires first clearing Normal End ED11『此岸と彼岸』. The corrected, cross-checked primary path chooses Day 1『わたしは首を横に振る』and Day 3『行ってきます』(XNEO + HD Remaster Lastcharles). Create the source-backed Save⑦/operational Save13 after『抵抗しない』BEFORE choosing『封じを強化する』; on the first ED11 pass the final『忘れたくない！』/『意識が―もう――』choice is still sealed and does not appear (independent Toppoi first-clear play note), so pass directly from『封じを強化する』to ED11. Then load Save13, use『鏡を探してみる → 割るのは忍びない』for a second ED11 needed for the Tsuzura-side Nozomi seal; reload for the unlocked『封じを強化する → 意識が―もう――』ED11 and finally『封じを強化する → 忘れたくない！』ED12. Livedoor's immediate mirror-first Save⑦ segment assumes a post-clear state; its sequential mirror-search and mirror-handling decisions are valid distinct events. ED8『蛇の神の使い』is shown as an explicit failed-run prefix using the fully enumerated HD Remaster no-sweets/well-marker route. That branch occurs before the first documented save, so the guide must restart Day 1 for the main run, not load a made-up checkpoint. XNEO/Livedoor document an alternative ED8 path with『負けてたまるか』after sweets; these are separate paths, not concatenated. ED10『言霊の継承(2)』uses XNEO's complete『これは夢だし → 別にそんなことは → サクヤさんに付き合う → 保護者同伴なら → でもひとりは嫌なんでしょ？ → 抵抗しない』low-affinity branch and Save④/operational Save10; the independent HD Remaster walkthrough lists a distinct sufficient low-affinity ED10 sequence『ん～？ → 気になる → 別にそこまでしなくても → サクヤさんに付き合う → 保護者同伴なら → でもひとりは嫌なんでしょう？』. Both lead ED10, but the guide emits one complete XNEO path. Foxtail separately documents ED10 condition choices but does not independently verify the guide's complete Save10 affinity/choice state; exact-target ED10 same-state reachability remains blocked. PS2 and HD Remaster remain treated as the same route system absent evidence of behavior changes; exact choices are source-reconciled, not executable-playtested. All seven source-documented Tsuzura saves are retained, numbered 7–13, without creating a new save before ED8.

routes.title: 浅間サクヤルート
routes.notes: Asama Sakuya (浅間サクヤ, VNDB c10499). Recommended after the required Uzuki/Tsuzura unlock work. True End is『ついのときまで』（ED25）; other documented endings are ED4/22-24/26-27. PS2 and HD Remaster are treated as the same route system. All five source-documented Sakuya checkpoints are preserved: global Save14=local①, Save15=local②, Save16=local③, Save17=local④, Save18=local⑤; the ED23/26/24/27 recovery graph remains the already-flattened reachable structure. ED4『雫』has multiple valid documented paths; the guide emits the complete Livedoor replay-from-beginning path, while Foxtail red6 and the supplementary walkthrough are recorded as alternative routes to the same ending rather than version-specific behavior. ED22 also has multiple valid routes: Livedoor and the supplementary walkthrough support direct『見ているしかなかった → ED22』, while XNEO/Foxtail/the supplementary walkthrough support『飛び出していた → 月は蝕まれる運命なんだ → ED22』. The guide emits only the direct『見ているしかなかった』route and does not concatenate the two alternatives; Foxtail's『見ているしかなかった(No.22へ)』supports that branch choice. ED24 uses『凍てる孤月』based on Livedoor + Foxtail; XNEO's『凍てる弧月』is an orthographic source variant. ED26 is retained as Normal End because XNEO + Foxtail agree; Livedoor's Bad-End label is treated as a classification error/outlier. ED23 source-state gate: the independent HD Remaster Lastcharles ED23 route explicitly prints『飛び出していた』after『各個撃破は愚の骨頂』, and the Livedoor Set-A ED23 recovery lists the same intermediate prompt (indexed text only; direct fetch unavailable). Foxtail's Set-B ED23 branch omits that prompt, while its same text occurs in another branch. Critically, the guide chooses『やめておく → 止める』before Save16, whereas Lastcharles's ED23 path explicitly chooses『待てーっ！ → 止めない』immediately before『各個撃破は愚の骨頂』. The Lastcharles intermediate prompt is therefore evidence for a different immediate decision state, not same-branch corroboration. XNEO's『止める』ED23 path omits that prompt. The current Save16 preceding state is not shown equivalent to Lastcharles, so the guide's ED23 detour remains unverified; the step's Set-B excerpt now comes from Lastcharles, not the unrelated Foxtail event.

routes.title: ユメイルート
routes.notes: Yumei (ユメイ, VNDB c10497). True End is『白花の咲く頃に』（ED21）; alternate endings are ED1/5/16-20. PS2 and HD Remaster are treated as the same route system. The emitted opening『わたしはこくりと頷いた → 気のせいだと思い込む』is supported by Livedoor + Foxtail; differing XNEO opening choices are treated as alternate valid routing rather than a release change. All seven documented Yumei saves remain preserved. Yumei precedes Nozomi because the actual Nozomi seal requires completing an ending after『だけど彼女たちだって可哀相』; XNEO's ED18 prerequisite wording is treated as shorthand for a route state that satisfies that underlying flag, not a different mechanic. ED20『赤い絆』is retained as Bad End from XNEO + Foxtail; Livedoor's Normal-End label is treated as a classification error/outlier. Current Y1/Y2 author correction: XNEO's 42 directly inspected Set-A choice excerpts use 〖...〗, not 【...】; Yumei steps 20/24/39 use Foxtail's printed ………… as the player-facing literal. XNEO directly prints the ED20 choice/condition at step 39, including its full arrow context; for optional ED18-branch steps 20 and 24 the directly inspectable XNEO excerpt does not document that exact event/state, so jpGuide1 uses the permitted Set-A omission placeholder rather than claiming unverified Livedoor quotation. ED21 Set-A heading preserves XNEO's three-line layout. Direct Switch-state verification and inaccessible Livedoor checkpoint/transcription evidence are not thereby certified.

routes.title: ノゾミルート
routes.notes: Nozomi (ノゾミ, VNDB c10502). PS2 and HD Remaster are treated as the same route system. The underlying route seal is the pair documented by Livedoor + Foxtail red5: complete an ending after Tsuzura-route『割るのは忍びない』and complete an ending after Yumei-route『だけど彼女たちだって可哀相』, opening『赤い縛め / 三日目 / 夜』. XNEO's Yumei-ED18 prerequisite is treated as shorthand/proxy for a prior route state that satisfies the Yumei-side seal, not a release-specific mechanic. The recommended order satisfies both flags before Nozomi. The route ends are Bad End『ニ重箱の底で』（ED14）and True End『光は風に』（ED15）;『ニ重箱』is retained from Livedoor + Foxtail, while differing orthography is treated as a source variant. No source designates ED15 as a single overarching true ending. Current accuracy blocker N1: The emitted Nozomi opening/night choices and Save26/Save① return are supported in Foxtail Set B and attributed to Livedoor Set A, but Livedoor currently times out on direct inspection. Directly inspectable XNEO Set A instead prints a different Nozomi opening/night route and does not corroborate the Save① checkpoint. Neither indexed snippets nor Foxtail alone establish the exact emitted two-set main path/save. Do not alter those choices or checkpoint speculatively; require directly inspectable independent Set-A evidence or a fully reconciled alternative before PASS.

sources.title: アカイイト完全攻略 | XNEO
sources.notes: Set A component. Detailed Japanese text walkthrough covering all five routes, prerequisites, choices, ending names/numbers, and many alternate-ending paths. Although written for the original PS2 release, the owner-approved reconciliation treats PS2 and HD Remaster as the same route system absent concrete behavioral-change evidence; XNEO is therefore reconciled directly with Livedoor and Foxtail rather than treated as an obsolete-version source. Where it differs, the difference is classified as an alternate valid path, shorthand/omitted state, transcription/orthography issue, or walkthrough error.

sources.title: アカイイト/アカイイトHD REMASTER　攻略まとめ
sources.notes: Set A component. Directly inspected Japanese walkthrough explicitly covering both the original PS2 game and アカイイト HD REMASTER. It is especially useful for numbered save/checkpoint positions and compact ending-recovery sequences, but its HD label does not give it automatic priority over XNEO/Foxtail. Under the same-route-system premise, its disagreements are reconciled as branch-state shorthand or source errors where the state tables disagree. Known examples: the Uzuki ED13 Save② shortcut combines incompatible state (and incorrectly emits the later night choice), Tsuzura ED11 presents sequential mirror-search and mirror-handling decisions, and its ED20/ED26 classifications are outliers.

sources.title: FAQ/アカイイト攻略FAQ - アカイイト/アオイシロ まとめwiki
sources.notes: Partial/supplementary source, not a complete walkthrough on its own. Its FAQ section documents three specific hard-to-find choice sequences that are easy to miss on the branch diagram (烏月ルート「吸血鬼」の左, 烏月ルート「どうしてこんなところに？」の左→左, 葛ルート「コドク」の左, サクヤルート「歓迎の心は掃除から」の左→右), given as full choice chains. These were cross-checked against xneo.jp's day-by-day listings and are consistent. Also confirms there is no single canonical 'grand happy end' bugfix and that a specific ending ('言霊の継承(2)') has a known freeze bug unrelated to route logic. Site required a direct fetch with a browser user-agent (returns HTTP 403 to generic fetchers).

sources.title: アカイイト - ゲームカタログ@Wiki ～名作からクソゲーまで～
sources.notes: Reference/review article, not a choice-by-choice walkthrough. Used to corroborate structural facts: total of 32 endings (5 happy/True Ends, 12 Normal Ends, 15 Bad Ends); confirms only Uzuki's route needs no prior unlock ('ルートの解除をせずにいきなりハッピーエンドに到達出来るのは烏月だけ'); explicitly states there is NO single 'true happy end' among the 5 heroine True Ends ('「真のハッピーエンド」が存在しない...本当の意味でのハッピーエンドが存在しない'), and that the sequel Aoishiro added a 'Grand Happy End' specifically in response to this criticism (implying Akai Ito itself, including the 2023 HD Remaster, was not given one). Also supports the owner-approved reconciliation premise: the 2023 Switch/Steam 'AKAIITO HD REMASTER' is a remaster of the same content/routes as the original 2004 PS2 release, with no new routes added; no concrete route-behavior change is documented. Retrieved via Wayback Machine snapshot (direct fetch returns HTTP 403) at http://web.archive.org/web/20250303014011/https://w.atwiki.jp/gcmatome/pages/4086.html.

sources.title: PS２版「アカイイト」で全てのエンディングを見ました。- ルーファスの日記
sources.notes: Supplementary/opinion source only, not a walkthrough (no choice text). A completionist's blog post about having seen all 32 endings. Notable for a claim that conflicts with the guide's neutral 'no true end' framing: the author personally argues Yumei's True End is 'probably' the game's real true ending because the official drama CD's epilogue continues from a state consistent with her route. This is a personal interpretation, not corroborated by any walkthrough site, and is documented under disagreements rather than used to set is_true_ending on any route.

sources.title: Akai Ito - VNDB entry v98
sources.notes: Reference only. Confirms release history: original PS2 release (2004-08/10), SuperLite 2000 budget re-release (2005), PSN download (2013), and the newest release, 'AKAIITO HD REMASTER' for Nintendo Switch and Steam/PC (2023-05-25), bundled with a HD Remaster of the sequel Aoishiro. The 2023 HD Remaster is the release targeted for this guide per project rules (most recent platform). Release-history reference only. No concrete evidence was found that the HD Remaster changed route/ending behavior; walkthrough disagreements are therefore not treated as version differences without separate behavioral evidence.

sources.title: AKAIITO HD REMASTER 攻略
sources.notes: Japanese Set B component for Tsuzura on AKAIITO HD REMASTER. Independently directly inspected: complete Day 1–3 ED11/ED12 path and ED11-first hidden-final-choice unlock; full alternative ED8 no-sweets/well-marker branch; full independent ED10 low-affinity alternative, ED7/ED9 and mirror ED11. Also supplementary for Uzuki ED13 and Sakuya ED4/22/23. For Sakuya ED23, its directly inspected HD Remaster route prints『各個撃破は愚の骨頂 → 飛び出していた → いいよ』, but its ED23 path explicitly selects『待てーっ！ → 止めない』immediately before『各個撃破は愚の骨頂』, while the guide's Save16 ED23 path selects『やめておく → 止める』. This is an opposite immediate branch, not just different earlier Day 1–4 history; it supports the literal prompt on Lastcharles's distinct route only, not same-state applicability. The exact guide target is Nintendo Switch HD Remaster; no source documents route branching differences against the same HD Remaster release on PC.

sources.title: アカイイト レビュー・感想 (Toppoi)
sources.notes: Supplementary original-game first-run Tsuzura play notes, directly inspected 2026-10-11. Explicitly records no final choice on first clear ('一度目は選択肢が出ない') after the seal-strengthening choice. Not a substitute for the two complete Japanese Set A/B route guides.

disagreements: Owner-approved reconciliation premise: treat the original PS2 release and アカイイト HD REMASTER as the same route/ending system unless a source provides concrete evidence that game behavior changed. The inspected sources provide no such evidence. Walkthrough disagreements are therefore resolved as alternative valid paths, omitted prerequisite state / abbreviated recovery instructions, transcription or orthography differences, or walkthrough errors—not speculative PS2-vs-HD mechanics. 1) There is no single overarching 'true ending'; each heroine has her own True End. 2) Opening-choice differences between XNEO and Livedoor/Foxtail are treated as alternate valid routing or transcription variants when they do not change the represented ending logic; the guide uses an internally reachable path supported by the active source set. 3) Nozomi unlock wording: XNEO's Yumei-ED18 prerequisite is shorthand/proxy; Livedoor + Foxtail expose the underlying Tsuzura『割るのは忍びない』+ ending and Yumei『だけど彼女たちだって可哀相』+ ending route-seal flags. 4) Uzuki ED13: the required earlier no-chase state is corroborated by XNEO, Foxtail, and the supplementary walkthrough. Foxtail explicitly says the later night choice is absent in that state, so Livedoor's Save②『別に → 歯磨きはオッケー？』recovery is a state-combining walkthrough error. XNEO/Lastcharles list a trailing phone choice after the no-chase route, but Foxtail marks『別に』itself No.13 and says the later prompt is suppressed; the guide therefore ends the ED13 replay after『別に』and treats the extra phone entry as over-specified recovery shorthand, not a release difference. 5) Sakuya ED4: Livedoor, XNEO/Foxtail red6, and the supplementary walkthrough document different valid paths to the same ED4. The guide emits one complete replay-from-beginning path and records the others as alternatives. 6) Sakuya ED22: there are at least two valid routes—direct『見ているしかなかった → ED22』(Livedoor + supplementary walkthrough; Foxtail marks the choice No.22) and『飛び出していた → 月は蝕まれる運命なんだ → ED22』(XNEO + Foxtail + supplementary walkthrough). The guide emits only the direct route; concatenating the two is incorrect. 7) ED26『月へ向かう蝶』: XNEO + Foxtail classify it Normal End; Livedoor says Bad End. This is treated as a Livedoor classification error/outlier, and the guide retains Normal End. 8) ED24『凍てる孤月』: Livedoor + Foxtail support『孤月』while XNEO prints『弧月』; this is treated as an orthographic source variant, not a version difference. 9) Tsuzura ED11:『鏡を探してみる』at『鏡の鬼』and the conditional follow-up『割るのは忍びない』at『積極攻勢』are sequential decision events, as documented by XNEO and Foxtail, not mutually exclusive alternatives. The guide correctly preserves both steps in that order. Livedoor prints『牝岸と彼岸』where XNEO + Foxtail support the target-facing『此岸と彼岸』; preserve Livedoor's spelling only in verbatim Set-A excerpts. 10) Yumei ED20『赤い絆』: XNEO + Foxtail classify it Bad End; Livedoor says Normal End. This is treated as a Livedoor classification error/outlier, and the guide retains Bad End. 11) Historical Saomix material remains provenance-only and is not part of the active verification gate. 12) Tsuzura Day 1/3 and first-clear sequencing: Earlier Livedoor opening『わたしはこくりと頷いた』+『保護者同伴なら』led the player to a bad/alternate ending rather than the expected ED11; the complete XNEO and Lastcharles normal route agrees on『わたしは首を横に振る』+『行ってきます』. After『抵抗しない』place operational Save13 at Livedoor's source-documented Save⑦ BEFORE『封じを強化する』. The first ED11 is reached without the still-sealed LAST choice (Toppoi), not by skipping『封じを強化する』and not by moving Save13 after ED11. After the first ED11, reload Save13 for unlocked mirror/optional seal ED11 and true ED12 variants. Livedoor's mirror-first passage describes an unlocked play state; XNEO's ED11 mirror route is likewise a post-unlock alternative.  13) Foxtail Tsuzura page could not be re-fetched in the 2026-10-11 browser environment. Previously recorded Foxtail research remains intact; the independent HD Remaster Lastcharles walkthrough was directly inspected and promoted as an additional Set-B component for the Tsuzura primary path instead of pretending Foxtail had been inspected now. 14) ED8: the XNEO/Livedoor『葛ちゃんと食べよう → 負けてたまるか』path is an alternative from the HD Remaster Lastcharles『夜食は美容の敵かも → 尾花ちゃんゴー！』route, which independently suppresses blood-contact state and documents the well marker. The guide selects the full Lastcharles ED8 path and uses a complete replay prefix, since the source-backed Save① occurs only after the main-path food choice; it does not pretend that a save after sharing food can restore a no-sweets state. 15) ED10: XNEO explicitly lists the full path through『保護者同伴なら → でもひとりは嫌なんでしょ？ → 抵抗しない』after『これは夢だし → 別にそんなことは → サクヤさんに付き合う』. The HD Remaster source lists a different low-affinity ED10 method involving『別にそこまでしなくても』; the guide emits XNEO's full single path rather than concatenating two different methods. Foxtail's branch-state table independently prints three of the emitted ED10 choices as conditions/decisions, but does not establish that its full prior affinity/choice state matches XNEO's emitted Save10 detour. The exact combined Switch HD Remaster ED10 state remains unverified; do not claim the three Set-B excerpts independently certify the complete detour. 16) First-pass seal: Toppoi https://toppoi.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-38.html independently records『一度目は選択肢が出ない』at the final Tsuzura decision; used as supplementary Japanese first-play evidence, not a substitute for XNEO/Lastcharles main-route Set A/B. 17) Sakuya ED23 S2: Lastcharles's directly inspected Japanese HD Remaster ED23 walkthrough lists『各個撃破は愚の骨頂 → 飛び出していた → いいよ』, documenting the intermediate prompt on its distinct『止めない』ED23 route, not on this guide's『止める』branch. Livedoor's indexed (not directly retrievable) Set-A Save③ ED23 recovery also prints it. XNEO and Foxtail's ED23 branch omit the intermediate prompt; Foxtail prints『飛び出していた』in another event/branch, so that Foxtail occurrence cannot be used as the ED23 Set-B excerpt. The route's step 40 now quotes Lastcharles verbatim in jpGuide2 and gives conditional guidance. The immediately preceding Day 4 branch is opposite: the guide takes『やめておく → 止める』before Save16, whereas Lastcharles's ED23 path takes『待てーっ！ → 止めない』before『各個撃破は愚の骨頂』. Thus Lastcharles verifies the literal intermediate text on its own different-state ED23 path but does not corroborate its appearance after the guide's『止める』state; XNEO's corresponding『止める』ED23 path omits it. No same-state Switch HD Remaster proof or explicit owner exception was found, so ED23 remains blocked; do not infer universal prompt presence/absence or mark an accuracy PASS. 18) Yumei Y1/Y2: The 42 Set-A bracket transcriptions were normalized to directly inspected XNEO 〖...〗 (including literal detour arrows); the three blood-related actions use Foxtail ………… rather than unsupported middle-dot strings. XNEO directly prints ED20's ………… branch; its excerpt does not establish the two optional ED18-prefix occurrences as the same preceding state, so those Set-A lanes are explicitly undocumented pending direct Livedoor access. The exact Switch glyphs/saved-state outcomes are not independently certified by this typography correction. 19) Nozomi N1: Foxtail documents the emitted Nozomi choices but no numbered checkpoint; XNEO documents a different path, while the claimed Livedoor Save① path is not currently directly inspectable (timeout). Preserve the unresolved main-route source gate and Save26 position until directly inspectable same-path Set-A evidence or a reconciled alternative is available.
